jobs.description:
SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans. With our technological savvy and fan-first attitude we’re simplifying and modernizing the ticketing industry.

As Counsel, Commercial and Product, you will help drive SeatGeek's growth on two fronts: facilitating deal negotiation and execution for our enterprise SaaS business, and partnering with our product teams to bring new features and experiences to market. You’ll work directly with business stakeholders across Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Operations and you’ll have real ownership from day one on a legal team that is still building the playbooks it will scale with.

What you'll do

Commercial

• Draft, negotiate, and structure complex enterprise SaaS and sponsorship agreements with major sports franchises and other strategic partners, managing deals from first draft through signature and working closely with our enterprise sales team and prospective clients

• Review, draft, and negotiate a wide variety of other commercial agreements and amendments, including analytics, product integration, licensing, professional services, and general vendor and operations agreements

• Lead negotiations directly with counterparties and their counsel, driving open issues to resolution and keeping deals moving on business timelines

• Create and update contract templates and playbooks as our business evolves and grows

• Help develop processes to ensure ongoing compliance with contractual commitments, and provide practical, solutions-oriented advice to help client teams navigate issues that arise in the customer relationship, such as service outages and SLA remedies

• Build strong, day-to-day relationships with our sales and business leaders as a responsive and reliable point of contact

Product

• Partner with product and business teams throughout all stages of product development, from ideation and design through testing and launch

• Proactively identify, analyze, and mitigate legal and regulatory risks at every stage of the product life cycle, balancing risk against business opportunity

• Provide commercially focused product counseling on product design, user flows, fan experience, and UX copy

• Advise on new products and features in the US and select international markets, including the evolving regulatory landscape for ticketing

• Establish and maintain product-related legal documentation, including terms of service, marketplace policies, and consumer-facing messaging

What you have

• J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school and admission to the New York bar, or eligibility to register as in-house counsel

• 3+ years of experience; law firm and in-house backgrounds both welcome, prior in-house exposure preferred, tech experience is a plus

• Strong transactional background, with a track record of drafting and negotiating complex agreements and running deals end to end

• Skilled, efficient drafter: you turn documents quickly and precisely and adapt as deal terms evolve

• Advanced problem-solving skills and excellent judgment - you’re able to quickly digest a problem, evaluate solutions, and then weigh options and recommend a clear path forward

• Ability to balance legal risk mitigation against key business objectives and risks

• Passion for solving legal problems with the ability to explain legal concepts to non-lawyers

• You are a clear communicator who explains legal risk to non-lawyers and works well across business and legal teams

Perks

• Equity stake

• Discretionary annual bonus

• Flexible work environment, allowing you to work as many days a week in the office as you’d like or 100% remotely

• A WFH stipend to support your home office setup

• Unlimited PTO

• Up to 16 weeks of fully-paid family leave

• 401(k) matching

• Student loan matching program

• Health, vision, dental, and life insurance

• Up to $25k towards family building, reproductive health services and Gender-affirming care

• $500 per year for wellness expenses

• Subscriptions to Headspace (meditation), Headspace Care (therapy), and One Medical

• $360 per quarter to spend on tickets to live events

• Annual subscription to Spotify, Apple Music, or Amazon music

The salary range for this role is $151,000 - $218,000 USD. This role is equity eligible. In addition, you may receive a discretionary annual bonus based on individual and company performance. jobs.title: Community Engagement and Advocacy Manager
jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
Thank you for considering Tailscale . If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

The Community Programs team creates the spaces, programs, and opportunities that help our community thrive. We're looking for a Community Engagement and Advocacy Manager to help us strengthen relationships with the people who use, build with, and advocate for Tailscale.

In this role, you'll own and grow three important areas of our community: the Tailscale Insiders advocacy program, our digital communities, specifically Discord and Reddit, and our Community Projects program.

You'll focus on creating meaningful opportunities for community members to connect, contribute, share their expertise, and be recognized for the work they do. Whether that's helping an Insider find their next speaking opportunity, bringing Tailscale staff into conversations on Discord, or showcasing an exciting community-built project, you'll help turn community participation into lasting relationships and advocacy.

You'll work closely with teams across Tailscale, including Developer Relations, Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Support, to connect community members with the right people, resources, and opportunities.

We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys working with people, understands what makes communities thrive, and can turn ideas into thoughtful, well-run programs. You don't need to be deeply technical, but you should be curious about technology and excited to learn from the people building with it.

Key Responsibilities

Insiders Advocacy Program

• Own the strategy, day-to-day operations, engagement, and ongoing growth of the Tailscale Insiders advocacy program.

• Build and maintain meaningful relationships with Insiders, understanding their interests, expertise, motivations, and how they want to participate in the Tailscale community.

• Develop recurring engagement opportunities that help Insiders connect with one another and with teams across Tailscale.

• Identify opportunities for Insiders to contribute through speaking engagements, technical content, community events, product feedback, testing, and other initiatives.

• Partner with internal teams to create clear pathways for Insiders to participate in company initiatives, ensuring opportunities are relevant and mutually beneficial.

• Identify and nurture emerging advocates across the Tailscale community, creating pathways for deeper participation and potential involvement in the Insiders program.

• Own the recruitment, onboarding, recognition, and ongoing engagement of Insiders, ensuring participants feel valued, supported, and connected.

• Gather feedback from program members and continuously improve the Insider experience.

• Track program participation, contributions, engagement, and outcomes to understand and communicate the impact of the program.

Digital Communities: Discord & Reddit

• Own the strategy, day-to-day engagement, and overall community experience across Tailscale's Discord and Reddit communities, fostering welcoming, active, and inclusive spaces.

• Develop and execute engagement initiatives, including community events, AMAs, discussions, and member spotlights that encourage participation and connection.

• Partner with teams across Tailscale to bring staff into community conversations and create opportunities for meaningful engagement.

• Partner with Product, Marketing, and Developer Relations to plan and lead Discord and Reddit engagement around product launches, announcements, and key company initiatives.

• Own day-to-day community moderation, including enforcing guidelines, managing moderation tools and bots, coordinating volunteer moderators, and escalating sensitive issues to appropriate internal teams.

• Identify opportunities to improve community engagement, structures, and experiences based on member feedback and participation.

• Recognize and celebrate active members and contributors, creating opportunities for deeper involvement and advocacy.

• Monitor community conversations, feedback, and engagement metrics to identify emerging themes, share actionable insights with internal teams, and inform community strategy, product decisions, and program improvements.

jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
About AppOmni

AppOmni is redefining SaaS security for the age of agentic security operations. As AI transforms the way security teams build, operate, and defend their environments, AppOmni is pioneering a new approach to securing the world’s most critical SaaS ecosystems.

From its roots as a leader in SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM), AppOmni is driving the next evolution of SaaS security - bringing intelligence, automation, and agentic capabilities into security operations. AppOmni empowers organizations to move beyond traditional visibility and posture management toward more intelligent, proactive, and autonomous security.

Recognized as a Frost Radar™ 2025 Leader and Great Place To Work ® , AppOmni continues to set the standard for innovation and customer value in SaaS security.

About the Role

This position in a rapidly growing security engineering company is an opportunity to own the architecture that lets the largest regulated enterprises adopt AppOmni. Our customers' security teams review our platform as closely as we review their SaaS applications, and they expect fine-grained access control, control over their encryption keys, least-privilege access to the SaaS applications we monitor, and a network and identity architecture they can trust.

As a Senior Architect, you will define how the AppOmni SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) platform meets those requirements across the application, identity and network layers. You will work with engineering teams to deliver it, and you will represent the architecture directly to customer security and architecture teams. These are hard problems in a multi-tenant platform, and your decisions will shape how the product is built for years.

What You'll Do

• Own the architecture for AppOmni's enterprise readiness capabilities and maintain a roadmap for them with Product.

• Design role-based access control for the platform, including custom roles, permissions scoped by SaaS application or business unit, and consistent enforcement across the UI, APIs and integrations.

• Design bring-your-own-key and customer-managed key support on Google Cloud KMS, extending our existing per-tenant envelope encryption, including key rotation, revocation and the effect on data availability.

• Define the OAuth and API access model for monitored SaaS applications, minimizing the permissions and scopes we request from each vendor, and work with SaaS vendors where their permission models fall short.

• Own identity integration requirements: SAML and OIDC single sign-on, SCIM provisioning, service accounts and API tokens, and session management.

• Be the authority on our network architecture on Google Cloud, including VPC design, private connectivity options, egress controls and static IPs for customer allowlisting, ingress protection, and service-to-service authentication in GKE.

• Strengthen tenant isolation and data protection across the platform, and review new services for security and enterprise readiness before they ship.

• Join customer architecture and security reviews, answer technical due diligence, and turn recurring customer requirements into platform features.

• Write architecture documents and reference designs, and mentor engineers on secure design.

What We're Looking For

• 12+ years in software engineering, security engineering or architecture, including 4+ years as an architect or principal-level engineer on a multi-tenant SaaS platform.

• Deep experience designing authorization systems (RBAC, ABAC or relationship-based models) for enterprise products.

• Hands-on experience with encryption and key management in the cloud, including envelope encryption, KMS, and customer-managed or externally held keys.

• Strong knowledge of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML and SCIM from both the identity provider and the application side.

• Strong cloud network security experience: VPC architecture, private connectivity, firewalls, egress control, TLS and mTLS, and zero-trust service access, ideally on Google Cloud.

• Experience taking a SaaS product through enterprise security reviews and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or FedRAMP.

• Ability to read and write production code in Python or Go and review designs down to the code level.

• Excellent written and verbal communication with engineers, executives and customer security teams.

• Experience working in a remote environment.

You Might Also Have

• Experience with Kubernetes and GKE security, including workload identity, network policies and service mesh.

• Experience with policy engines such as OPA or Cedar, or Zanzibar-style authorization services such as SpiceDB.

• Experience with the admin and permission models of enterprise SaaS platforms such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, ServiceNow or Workday.

• Experience serving financial services or other highly regulated customers, including data residency requirements.

jobs.description:
Overview

CoinTracker is on a mission to unlock everyone's financial potential so they can build the life they want. We started with crypto, building the tax and portfolio tools that millions of users trust to trade digital assets with peace of mind. Nino builds the next layer of financial fluency for our users. Nino is an AI-powered financial operating system that makes comprehensive, expert-level tax and financial planning advice accessible.

More on Nino : Comprehensive tax and financial planning strategies are currently locked behind high AUM fees or require enough wealth to have a family office. We are turning expert judgment into software so we can serve millions. AI is going to redefine how people understand their finances and how tax advice gets delivered. Not in ten years, in 2026. You can help define that, or spend the next few years adapting to rules someone else wrote. Nino sits inside CoinTracker ($100M raised, partnered with Coinbase, TurboTax, H&R Block, and Thomson Reuters) with the autonomy of an early-stage startup and the reach of an established platform.

Your mission

As Tax Lead, you'll own a book of roughly 50 Nino clients end-to-end: preparing, reviewing, and filing their returns and giving them proactive, white-glove tax advice.

Most of your time goes to client and compliance work, using our in-house AI tools alongside traditional tax software.

Along the way, you'll share what you learn with our engineers, so the logic in your head (ISO exercises, AMT crossover points, multi-state allocation, Roth conversions) makes our AI smarter for every household after yours. Product experience is a plus.

When we're done, the tax planning advice we'll provide won't just be static advice delivered once a quarter. It will execute, perform, and action personalized advice to each customer in a way that is simply not possible with legacy tax planning.

Location: U.S. remote.

Your one-year outcomes

•
Manage 50 to 60 clients end-to-end with excellence.

What you will do

•
Interface with Clients: Proactive tax insights and white-glove experience.

•
Prepare, review, and file tax returns for households (starting with those in $1M – $25M net worth) plus related business returns.

•
Share your tax logic: relay learnings from client work so engineers can turn your reasoning into product.

•
Review AI output: check and correct AI-generated advice before it reaches your clients.

•
Solve Edge Cases: AMT crossover, wash sales, multi-state allocation, QSBS, pass-through optimization.

What we look for

•
Role-agnostic

•
Opportunity alignment: You want to bring expert tax and financial advice to households that have outgrown doing it themselves, and you want to do it at an early-stage company where your work moves the number.

•
High agency: You see what needs doing and do it. You don't wait for a brief, a budget, or an engineer.

•
Exceptional collaboration: You make the people around you better: sales, advisors, engineers, and agencies. You say what you think and follow through.

•
First-principles thinking: You start from how customers decide, not from a playbook. You can explain why a number moved.

•
Role-specific

•
5+ years with an active CPA license. You've prepared, reviewed, and/or filed 500+ individual (1040) returns.

•
You've served clients with $1M – $25M net worth.

•
You have working knowledge of business returns (S-corps, partnerships, Schedule C, LLC).

•
You know the tax code, not just the tax software. You research ambiguous positions using primary sources (IRC, Treasury Regs, Rev. Rulings, case law) and can defend them.

•
You're AI native, with hands-on use of AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT.

•
Bonus: you're a tax attorney or CFP, or you have experience with trusts and estate planning.

The starting salary for this position is between $137,000 - $162,000 USD. Candidate's location does not impact the posted salary range.

The actual compensation offered will be based on a variety of job-related factors including relevant skills, education, and experience. This position also includes equity in CoinTracker and benefits like medical, dental, vision, 401(k), life insurance, and PTO.

About Enode

The grid was built for predictable, centralised power. Today it's absorbing intermittent supply from grid scale solar and wind, alongside dynamic demand from EVs, heat pumps, and home batteries. The missing piece is software that can connect and orchestrate these devices at scale.

We’re the layer between the home and the grid. Our platform connects every asset, coordinates every home and shapes thousands as one. Asset connectivity gives energy retailers one API for 1,000+ device models across 100+ brands. Home energy coordination turns that connection into smarter behavior at home, like charging an EV in the cheapest hours or using more of your own solar. Residential flexibility brings connected homes together into a dispatchable resource the grid can count on.

Europe’s largest energy companies build on Enode : retailers, utilities and the teams that trade for them. The platform spans 1.7M+ connected households and 5,000+ MW of controllable load. We’re backed by Y Combinator, Lowercarbon Capital and Creandum.

The decisions made now will shape how the next grid gets built. We’re looking for people who take ownership, think clearly under complexity and care deeply about the craft of building software that matters.

AI is fundamental to how we work

AI is how a team our size keeps rewiring the way we work, fast enough to match what our mission demands. We look for people who reach for AI as a reflex and who can drop a habit that used to work. People who care about unblocking others, not just about what they ship themselves. If that's not quite how you work yet but it's the direction you're heading, we'd still like to hear from you. We assess this in our interview process, alongside everything else we look at.

What we're looking for:

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer for our new Deployment team. The team works inside Europe's largest energy retailers, deep in their software architecture, to turn Enode's platform into infrastructure that enables steering large fleets of residential load. A retailer's charging data arrives in several formats from a few legacy systems and their team has been blocked for weeks: you are the person who unblocks them.

You'll join as one of the first members of the team, working directly with our Head of Deployment, Ben Brandt. There is no playbook yet, and you'll help write it. Every deployment should make the next one faster.

No sales experience? Good. That's not what we're hiring for.

Most people you'll call didn't ask to hear from you. They're running construction sites, chasing programmes and fighting fires, and they'll give you about ten seconds to prove you're worth two minutes. Earn those two minutes, find a real problem, and you'll be opening doors at some of the UK's biggest construction firms.

You don't need a sales CV for this. You need to be curious, resilient and genuinely coachable. We'll teach you the rest, with a proper 90-day plan, a coach alongside you every week, and a playbook built from the calls that are actually winning.

It won't always be easy, but you'll learn faster than almost anywhere else. If you'd rather be genuinely good at sales in two years than comfortable in two months, keep reading.

(this will be a long write up but we like to give you all the details before you spend your time applying)

_________________________________________________________________________________________

We are Shape.Construction!

We are digitising the largest and most fundamental industry in the world, the industry that literally builds the foundations of the civilisation we all depend on to spare us from a brutal hunter-gatherer life: CONSTRUCTION

It is one of the least digitised industries in the world but also the largest – 1 in 9 people globally work in the construction industry and it constitutes 11% of global GDP.

Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. ( Watch our short film about it).

We got our start as a high-end construction project management consultancy. As a consultancy, we are focused on genuinely upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. We then take the deep understanding of the projects we work on to develop construction management software products that anyone can use to deliver their projects better.

We are building a full suite of products one module at a time – kind of like office 365 but for construction management - Check out Shape, our construction management tech

The core of all this is our true secret sauce; people. We only recruit the very best both in capability and personality. We are deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that is optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People that join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined.

This approach has allowed us to grow from just 2 people in 2017 to over 220 today (including consultancy) and we are still very much at the beginning! Joining us isn't just some "job", it is a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life.

4 core values for a good life

We believe a life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships with others and challenging yourself to create a positive impact. So our values reflect the 4 levels of relationships that each of us has:

• Grow yourself – Your relationship with yourself

• Care about people – Your relationship with others around you

• Execute to greatness – Your relationship with your team

• Build civilisation – Your relationship with humanity and the world

This goes much deeper but for the sake of brevity, we will keep the summary version!

We enshrined our values in our vision

We exist so that everyone in our team can thrive in a high-impact community that:

• Connects us with meaningful relationships

• Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans

• Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures

We believe that, by first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.

And enable the achievement of our vision through our dual missions:

• To fully digitise the construction of human civilisation

• To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society

_________________________________________________________________________________________

The Role

Purpose of the role

You're where every Shape deal starts: finding the right people at construction firms and booking qualified meetings that turn into free launches and contracts. It's a role for someone who wants to learn sales properly, from the ground up, in a team that cares about doing it well.

What the job actually is

Most of your day, every day, is on the phone. You'll be calling commercial, project and operations leaders at tier 1 and tier 2 construction firms (main contractors and the subcontractors who work for them). They're running live projects, their time is precious and they're wary of anyone selling software. You'll hear "no", "not now" and "just send me an email" a lot. Almost all of our pipeline is outbound, apart from customer referrals, so the meetings you book are ones you've created yourself.

Quality over quantity, always. We care about the work we do and take pride in doing it properly, and we're looking for people who feel the same. On

At Clover, the Business Enablement team leads our technological advancement while ensuring robust security and compliance. We’re hiring a Engineering Lead to build the systems that help our clinical teams deliver services in the field and in members’ homes. You will own technical direction and delivery for scheduling, dispatch, field and mobile workflows, and the software that connects equipment and home technology to the operation.

A likely first assignment is an “Air Traffic Control” system for field operations. A supervisor needs to understand what is happening and act when the plan breaks: a flat tire, a delayed visit, a missing piece of equipment, or a member whose availability changes. You will work with the people doing the job to decide what they need to see, what the system can help resolve, and when a human should intervene.

This is a hands-on role that spans product and engineering. You will understand the business problem, shape the solution, build useful increments, and see whether they work. You may start without direct reports and can expect to coach and eventually manage one or two engineers. You should enjoy building personally and helping others become more capable.

We value a tinkering instinct: try the unfamiliar tool, inspect the data, trace the failure, put a small improvement in front of a user, and learn from what happens. Hardware or connected-device experience can be a strong signal of that mindset, but it is not required. The central work is building dependable software for an operation that changes throughout the day.

As an Engineering Lead, Clinical Operations, you will:

• Work directly with supervisors, clinical field staff, and operations leaders to understand schedules, travel, capacity, handoffs, and the exceptions that disrupt a day’s work.

• Build field visibility and intervention tools that give supervisors useful context, distinguish current facts from missing information, and help them respond to changing conditions.

• Develop scheduling and dispatch capabilities that match people and visits to practical constraints, with clear ways for operating staff to review and adjust the plan.

• Build and debug APIs, mobile workflows, integrations, and data flows supporting field teams, connected equipment, and home technology.

• Prototype quickly and ship focused increments. Make deliberate choices about what to build, integrate, or buy, and avoid committing to a large system before the operation has tested the approach.

• Use AI actively for development, investigation, prototypes, analysis, and useful workflow capabilities. Check the behavior and make failures understandable and recoverable.

• Coach engineers and take on a small number of direct reports as the team develops. Maintain clear ownership, sound engineering practices, and credible delivery commitments.

• Partner with Product, Special Project Leads, IT, Counterpart, and the Engagement lead at the interfaces their work shares with field operations.

Success in this role looks like:

• First 90 days: You understand how the field operation works, have shipped an improvement used by supervisors or field staff, and can show what it changed. You have a focused technical plan grounded in real constraints and exceptions.

• First six months: Several useful increments are in place. Supervisors can understand and respond to disruptions more effectively, scheduling and field workflows are improving, and technical ownership is clear.

You should get in touch if:

• You are a strong production software engineer who has owned meaningful work end-to-end and still builds regularly.

• You can move across backend services, APIs, data flows, user interfaces, and operational workflows to solve a real problem.

• You have strong product instincts, learn unfamiliar domains directly, and enjoy working with the people using what you build.

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain or Ireland.

The Opportunity

About our platform

Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely.

The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads.

About the Infrastructure group

We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable.

You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group.

We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen.

How we work

Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on.

Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it.

What You'll Be Doing

• Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth.

• Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity.

• Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them.

• Work across team boundaries, contributing beyond your squad's scope where Foundations needs it.

Operating across 12 Western states, our organization is dedicated to safeguarding residential properties, commercial sites, communities, and critical infrastructure from the destructive impact of wildfires.

As wildfires rapidly intensify across the West, they threaten communities and destabilize property insurance markets—creating a vital need and a powerful market opportunity for proven structural defense solutions. Beyond our core technology, Frontline is strategically positioning itself to capture high-growth adjacent opportunities, including strategic insurance partnerships and municipal fire service integration.

This performance has earned notable industry honors, including recognition as one of TIME Magazine’s Best Inventions, the National Association of Homebuilders IBS Best Home Technology of 2025, and recognition in Inc. Magazine’s ranking of the fastest-growing enterprises in the Pacific Region.

Frontline was founded by Harry Statter and is headquartered in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Frontline maintains a modern, flexible corporate culture supported by a predominantly distributed workforce. We welcome inquiries from qualified professionals seeking to contribute to a high-growth enterprise dedicated to preserving lives and property.

Frontline is seeking a strategic, operationally minded Chief Financial Officer to lead our finance function and help drive the company’s next phase of growth. In 1851, a New York bookkeeper named George D. Lyman observed the same absurd ritual each afternoon: porters carried bags of coins and bundles of checks bank to bank down Wall Street, settling by hand, a fortune exposed to error and theft. Lyman's fix: send everything through one central office and settle the net. On October 11, 1853, in the basement of 14 Wall Street, 52 banks cleared $22.6 million in a single sitting. Money between banks had stopped being an event and became seamless infrastructure.

The bank account is where a company's financial life happens - payroll clears or it doesn't; a wire lands or a deal slips; the month closes clean, or someone loses a weekend to it. Backed by Y Combinator and Sequoia Capital, Magic has spent 10+ years connecting fast-growing businesses with top remote talent.

This is a full-time, in-house, permanent role with full benefits. You'll be a Magic employee owning client relationships on the company's behalf, not a VA placed with a client. Our clients are busy founders and executives who need remote workers to deliver real ROI, and they need a strategic partner to make that happen. You're not here to answer tickets. You're here to protect revenue, grow accounts, and turn happy clients into loud advocates. The pace is live and constant: client calls, escalations, and account health across a real portfolio, every single day, with no handoffs and no delays.

Shift: US Eastern hours, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM ET, Monday to Friday (a 9-hour shift), with occasional early or late calls for West Coast clients or urgent situations. Fully remote, Philippines-based.

Key Responsibilities

•
Guard your book of business: own a portfolio of accounts sorted by size, health, and growth potential, and hold 90%+ gross revenue retention (GRR) and 110%+ net revenue retention (NRR). Those are the numbers you're graded on.

•
Spot at-risk accounts before clients say a word. Start renewals 60–90 days out, and get save plans moving early.

•
Launch every new client fast: kickoff call within 24–48 hours of signing, then Magic's 30-60-90 day onboarding framework, with a success plan tied to their business goals and an intro to their remote worker.

•
Host quarterly business reviews (QBRs) clients actually look forward to: data-driven, strategic, action-oriented. Become the trusted advisor to founders and C-suite, and multi-thread across each client so one champion leaving doesn't sink the account.

•
Hunt expansion opportunities and make the business case before anyone asks.

•
Surface the story in the data: track churn risk and expansion signals, keep HubSpot clean, send a monthly portfolio health report (retention, NRR, CSAT, NPS, QBR completion), and own every escalation from intake to resolution.

Qualifications & Technical Requirements

• 3+ years of B2B customer success or account management experience, juggling a portfolio of accounts at the same time

• Direct ownership of revenue retention and expansion targets across the full customer lifecycle from onboarding to renewal

• Background in SaaS/tech, outsourcing/staffing, professional services/BPO, or marketplace platforms

• HubSpot experience used daily for pipeline and account health (intermediate-to-expert Salesforce or a similar CRM also works)

• Intermediate-to-advanced Excel or Google Sheets: pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX MATCH, dashboards, trend analysis

• Real US market experience: you know US business culture, SMB challenges, and how executives like to communicate

• Strong written and spoken English, good enough for daily conversations with US-based C-level and Director clients

• A professional home office: high-speed internet (50+ Mbps), a headset, and a quiet space

You treat customer success as a revenue function, not a help desk. You own the outcome, so you don't wait to be told an account is wobbling; you've already spotted it, and your save plan is moving. You're comfortable in a room with a founder or a C-suite exec, and you can plow through a messy escalation without losing the relationship. You read the data, find the story, and walk into every QBR with a point of view. You pitch expansion because the numbers back it up, not because a quota told you to. When something breaks, you adapt, get the right people in the room, and keep going.

Application + pre-qualifying questions → HR interview (45 min) → 24-hour reflection period → Panel Interview with Senior CSMs → interview with CS Director → Final Interview with the Head of Sales & CS → Job Offer

What's In It For You
₱60,000–₱80,000 gross per month, permanent and full-time, fully remote (Philippines). HMO coverage after regularization, 12 vacation days and 10 sick days a year, 13th month pay, SSS, PhilHealth, and PAG-IBIG. We offer paid training and promote from within: top CSMs move into Senior CSM, Team Lead / CS Manager, and CS Director roles.

We're an ambitious, driven team that plows through obstacles instead of waiting for perfect conditions. There's no hierarchy and no politics: you can talk to anyone, on any team, about anything. We respect each other's time, and we actually like working together. Magic is backed by Y Combinator and Sequoia Capital, with more than 10 years of connecting top remote talent with fast-growing businesses and 2,000+ remote workers worldwide.

If you lead with Design Craft, live at the frontier of AI for brand and creative, and want to build systems that help a whole company look and sound like one brand, this role is for you.

What we value

• Design Craft with speed — You hold high standards and know how to hit deadlines.

• Curiosity about what's next — You stay on the leading edge of brand and creative, from new AI tools to new techniques, and you share what you learn.

• AI-native by default — You reach for AI first, test what works on real projects, and teach others how.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: EMEA - Remote, UNITED STATES - Remote

Please note that we are unable to consider applications from candidates based in France, Italy, or Germany for this role.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About MetaMask

MetaMask is building a future where users can unlock the full product stack through a single, seamless identity experience, enabling access to all features with trust, safety, and minimal friction.

Today, identity verification is fragmented across several product and onboarding experiences. Users are repeatedly asked to verify themselves across different services, creating unnecessary friction, inconsistent outcomes, and degraded trust.

Universal KYC (UKYC) is a new initiative to solve this problem by creating a single, reusable identity layer across MetaMask. At the centre of this is MetaMask Passport , a product designed to enable users to verify once and unlock multiple experiences across the MetaMask ecosystem.

This role sits at the intersection of platform and product experience . You will define the primitives, standards, and user journeys that make identity verification seamless, privacy-conscious, and globally compliant.

What you’ll do

You will own the vision and roadmap for Universal KYC and MetaMask Passport, defining how a reusable identity layer unlocks the broader MetaMask product stack. You will build the underlying identity platform, creating scalable verification primitives and standards that can be adopted across products. In parallel, you will design a seamless, low-friction KYC experience that reduces time-to-first-transaction while maintaining compliance integrity. You will drive adoption across MetaMask by partnering closely with internal teams to integrate a consistent identity layer, while balancing privacy, trust, and global regulatory requirements. Throughout, you will lead execution end-to-end, aligning cross-functional teams and delivering measurable outcomes.

What we are looking for:

• Proven experience building or scaling identity verification (IDV), KYC, or onboarding products

• Strong background in fintech , ideally with exposure to Web3

• Hands-on experience working with identity verification providers (IDV vendors) such as Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido, Persona, or Stripe Identity

• Familiarity with compliance workflows , including KYC, KYB, and customer due diligence (CDD) processes

• Track record of delivering platform products adopted across multiple teams

• Ability to operate across both technical systems and user experience

What Success looks like:

• Increased KYC completion rates and reduced onboarding friction

• Reduced time-to-first-transaction across KYC-gated flows

• Increased reuse of verified identity across products

• Improved transaction success rate through consistent verification outcomes

• Strong user trust with minimal friction and compliant execution

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, based in Poland, you'll build backend systems that help GitLab engineers trust the software they create with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but passing tests don't always mean the software works as intended. You'll contribute to validation approaches and feedback mechanisms that help agents catch that gap and self-correct while they work.

This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We’re looking for someone who has built with agents, run into the gap between passing tests and working software, and wants to help close it.

• Own backend features from design through production rollout, making the design calls within the architecture the team agrees on.

• Implement feedback that helps agents identify problems and self-correct during development.

• Backend development experience in at least one of Rust, Ruby, Go, or Python, with openness to working across languages.

• Experience taking backend features from design into production, discussing implementation trade-offs, and knowing when to ask for guidance.

• Comfort working inside a large existing codebase, not only on greenfield projects.

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

The client is a pair of sister engineering and technical support businesses serving the UK industrial, energy, and offshore sectors. Led commercially by their Commercial Director and supported by their technical leadership, both companies operate with a relationship-first approach—rejecting high-volume, pushy telesales in favor of consultative partnerships that solve genuine operational, resourcing, and project mobilisation challenges.
While operating as distinct brands with equal commercial priority, they share a unified mission: connecting UK industrial and energy clients with specialized engineering expertise, technical labour, and project support.

• Brand A (Technical Resourcing): Focuses on technical resourcing, engineering support, and solving skilled labour shortages across industrial and energy projects.

• Brand B (Engineering & Mobilisation): Delivers specialized engineering, technical scoping, and project mobilisation services—including offshore and broader industrial operations.

ROLE OVERVIEW:

This is a dedicated, full-time outbound B2B (Business-to-Business) relationship-building role reporting directly to the Commercial Director. The representative is responsible for researching prospect lists, engaging key decision-makers across UK (United Kingdom) businesses, and uncovering genuine operational, labour, or project needs across two sister engineering and technical support companies equally—rather than relying on pushy, script-based telesales. Ultimately, the role acts as a strategic gatekeeper who protects leadership's time by qualifying opportunities and handing over well-researched, high-value meetings to the Commercial Director, supported technically by the offshore operations lead and wider engineering team.

Key Responsibilities:

• Work through the prospect lists for both businesses and find the person who actually makes or influences the buying decision.

• Pick up the phone, introduce the clients properly, and have a sensible conversation about the work the company does and any help it may need.

• Ask good questions about upcoming projects, busy periods, labour shortages, existing suppliers, and who is responsible for buying support.

• Build relationships over time. Follow up by phone and email without pestering people or using a generic sales script.

• Keep the client contact records up to date. If a company is relevant to both, flag it and coordinate the approach so we do not contact them twice unnecessarily.

• Book meetings for the client when there is a real reason for him to speak to the prospect, then send him a clear note before the meeting.

When a meeting is ready for the client:
The client has commitments and is often working offshore, so we need to protect their time. The BDE should not book a meeting just because someone agrees to a chat. Before handing it over, we would expect them to know:

• Who we are speaking to and what they are responsible for.

• What the company is working on and which Company A or Company B service might help.

• Whether there is a genuine need, an upcoming requirement or a sensible reason to stay in touch.

• What the next conversation with Martin is supposed to achieve.

The handover should be short and useful: company, contact details, project or site, what the prospect has told us, likely services, timing and agreed next steps. The client will take the commercial relationship forward. And the other manager and the relevant technical people will get involved where we need their experience on resourcing, scope, or mobilisation.

• Confident spoken and written English, with a clear and friendly telephone manner that works well with UK businesses.

• Previous experience making outbound B2B calls and finding the right decision-makers.

• Engineering, recruitment, or industrial experience would be useful, but is not essential if they can learn quickly.

• Someone who listens, asks sensible questions and can talk naturally without reading from a script.

• Organised and persistent, with good follow-up habits and accurate notes in Excel or a CRM.

• Reliable working from home, with a quiet space, good internet and the ability to work a full-time week during UK business hours.

• Someone who wants to be part of our businesses and build accounts over time, rather than move from one short-term calling campaign to another.

• Work from Home

• UK Business Hours

GaggleAMP is a profitable SaaS company that has led the employee-advocacy category for over a decade. We're hiring our second Account Executive: a full-cycle closer who builds their own pipeline, qualifies hard, sells on value and holds price.

• Qualification. Confirm fit, find the person who controls the budget and build a value case before you invest your time. Walk away quickly when those aren't there.

• Value-led discovery. Tie our impact to the buyer's own numbers, such as pipeline generated from social or paid spend we offset, before price comes up.

• Price. We don't discount. You sell at list price and let poor-fit deals go.

• You disqualify without drama. A clean no is a good outcome, and you can tell us about a recent deal you walked away from.

• You build value cases in dollars from what the buyer tells you. When a buyer has no hard number, you can still put a dollar value on reach and traffic.

• You tie price to value instead of defending it or offering a discount.

• You advance deals on buyer commitment, not because a call went well or a demo got booked.

• You understand the importance of getting to the decision maker to close deals.

• You get leverage from your tools. You use AI tools (such as ChatGPT or Claude) and prospecting tools (such as Apollo) every week to sell smarter.

• You have carried and closed a new-business quota, running deals yourself from discovery to signature.

• You have sold at a small or lean company and have sourced your own pipeline. Here, we target a 50/50 inbound/outbound split.

• Medical, Dental & Vision insurance (after 30 days).

• Join an exciting and dynamic company with a strong leadership team and culture.

• Grow professionally by gaining powerful experience managing relationships in the digital marketing space.

• Have the opportunity to contribute and directly impact the growth and direction of the company you work for.

We never ask about your current or past salary.

jobs.description:

About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Customer Digital Experience Team

Customer Digital Experience sits within the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer Success organization.

Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it.

Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to.

We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together.

About the Role

As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change.

It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone.

You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built.

If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on.

Responsibilities

• Build the lifecycle communication program end-to-end across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, from strategy through copy, build, launch, and iteration

• Create programs that serve the full customer base while working hardest for digital-only customers, and decide where messaging should differ for accounts with a dedicated team

• Collaborate directly with product, design, engineers, design partners, and users to shape scope and make practical trade-offs.

• Coordinate multi-person projects across the team and communicate decisions clearly in GitLab's asynchronous, all-remote environment.

• Mentor other engineers and contribute to technical direction across the Plan group and related artificial intelligence initiatives.

• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

jobs.sourceName: RSS: We Work Remotely: All Jobs
jobs.description:
Headquarters: United States - Remote, EMEA - Remote

Please note that we are unable to consider applications from candidates based in France, Italy, or Germany for this role.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About this role

We’re looking for a Senior Design Engineer to join the Consensys Design team, supporting MetaMask - the most used wallet in crypto. This is a rare opportunity to bring beautiful, intuitive experiences to millions of users engaging with decentralized applications and Web3 technologies every day.

As a Senior Design Engineer, you'll turn complex flows into simple and delightful experiences across our app and browser extension. Working closely with designers, engineers, and product managers, you'll take ideas from prototype to production - sweating the animations, haptics, and micro-interactions that make every interaction feel considered, not just functional. You'll build in React and React Native with an eye for pixel-perfect execution, contribute to our design system, and build agentic workflows that help the team move faster without cutting corners. If you love making complex things feel simple, care about craft down to the smallest detail, and want that craft in the hands of 30M+ users, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

In one sentence: Make MetaMask interactions feel intuitive, fast, and delightful - across mobile and extension

• Build pixel-perfect interfaces in React and React Native, with obsessive attention to detail.

• Design and implement animations and micro-interactions that make every tap feel considered.

• Translate Figma designs into accessible, production-ready experiences with minimal handoff friction.

• Build agentic workflows and tooling that speed up design-to-code and day-to-day engineering work.

• Grow the MetaMask design system: reusable, accessible components built to scale across platforms.

• Move from idea to prototype fast and validate with real users.

• Push for craft everywhere - the small animation nobody asked for that makes an interaction click.

Key Experience

• Portfolio demonstrating delightful, polished interfaces and interactions - not just static screens, but the motion and detail that make them feel alive.

• Proven track record shipping high-traffic, consumer-facing products in React and React Native.

• Fluency in modern JS/TypeScript and cross-platform frontend architecture: performance, accessibility, and scalable UI patterns

• An eye for interaction design and motion - you know when animations and haptics earn their place and when they're just noise.

• Strong Figma literacy - you read a design file like code.

• Good judgment about when to polish and when to ship.

• Comfortable working autonomously across a distributed, global team

• Hands-on experience with crypto wallets, blockchain, or related Web3 products.

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. While we have a pretty good idea of what we need, we're ready for you to challenge our thinking on who needs to be in this role .
The salary range listed for this role applies to US-based candidates only. Compensation for candidates based outside the US (including Canada, EMEA, and LATAM) will be determined based on location, experience, and skills during the interview process, and may differ from the listed US range.

$149,000 — $210,000 USD

We are committed to ensuring that our technology empowers people and communities through decentralized technologies. We welcome the range of perspectives and differences and celebrate them. Joining Collibra's AI Sales team

Collibra's AI Sales team is at the forefront of how enterprises adopt and scale AI, selling a suite of AI products including AI Command Center, Collibra Units, and Deasy Labs, Collibra's unstructured data platform for AI, directly to the builders and technical leaders driving production AI systems. Deasy Labs, part of Collibra, develops technology that automatically discovers, enriches, and maintains the semantic context inside unstructured data. Enterprise knowledge often lives in documents, PDFs, reports, and transcripts that traditional data systems cannot easily organize or govern. The Deasy platform analyzes that content and generates structured metadata, taxonomies, and relationships that allow AI systems to retrieve the right information with accuracy and control.

You have

• A bachelor's degree or equivalent related working experience is required

At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

• Openness - Your default is to be open. You're willing to share information, understand other perspectives, and consider new possibilities. You’re curious, ask open questions, and are receptive to thoughts and feedback from others.

• Grit - You demonstrate grit by having the courage to commit and persevere. You’re committed, earnest, and dive in to get the job done well with a positive attitude.

• Integrity - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You’re honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.

• Simplicity - Be like Einstein: “Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.”

• A minimum of 2 years experience in an Account Exec

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

Celonis grew up with the private sector: Deutsche Telekom, Mercedes-Benz, Uniper and three quarters of the DAX companies rely on Celonis Process Intelligence. Now we are taking the next big step in Germany: scaling our business with the public sector. To make this happen, Celonis is investing heavily through 2029 in its German public sector business.

Over the past year, we have built our Public Sector team from the ground up. Today, a strong go-to-market core team of Account Executives and Value Engineers is in place, working with federal and state-level institutions.

The police are one of our primary target organizations in the public sector. Police officers spend a large proportion of their time on data work and comparatively little on the actual investigation. We want to turn that around. With our new police solution, Metropolis, we help police authorities connect and make sense of their data, so that officers can focus on what matters most: solving cases and keeping people safe .

To address this, we are now complementing our existing Public Sector team with a highly specialized Account Executive who brings first-hand experience from inside the organization we serve: the Police .

The Role:

This is not a typical Account Executive role. You bring the perspective of someone who knows police work from the inside: how investigations really run, where time is lost in data work, and how decisions are made and budgets are approved. You will use this credibility to build trusted relationships with police authorities at federal and state level and position Celonis as a long-term partner for their digital transformation.

Working closely with our Public Sector AEs, Value Engineers and product experts, you will translate the operational reality of police work into compelling use cases, contribute to the creation of solution blueprints, drive opportunities from first conversation to signed contract, and help shape how Celonis enters and grows in this market.

• Bring the voice of the police into Celonis: share insights with our product, marketing and value engineering teams to sharpen our offering.

About the Organization

Millions of Americans feel politically homeless and left out of the two-party structure. Too many electoral choices are settled before most voters have a meaningful say, and our political system consistently fails to address the nation's biggest challenges. We are a stealth team building an ambitious cross-partisan political venture to make American democracy more open, competitive, and responsive. We will build the infrastructure to effectively challenge the two-party political establishment, and create fundamentally new pathways to elected office and engaged citizen participation.

Our first major initiative will launch publicly in spring 2027 with the objective of materially influencing the 2028 national election cycle. This project will combine the scale of a mainstream consumer technology product, the reach of a modern media operation, and the ground game of a national political campaign - complete with digital and IRL field organizing across dozens of states - to engage tens of millions of Americans and build a constituency that outlasts this election cycle.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Montreal, Quebec, Canada

URL: https://www.sweatpantsagency.com/

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.

•
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.

•
Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.

•
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.

Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

Working closely with our US Sales and global marketing teams, you’ll design programs that engage enterprise decision-makers and strengthen strategic customer relationships. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. • Clear communication skills, and the ability to influence engineering and finance stakeholders without direct authority

• FinOps Certified Practitioner certification and/or relevant cloud certifications are a plus.

• Financial and engineering fluency - able to translate technical architecture decisions into financial impact, and financial goals into technical action.

• Analytical rigor - comfortable working with large datasets to surface insights, quantify opportunities, and prioritize by impact.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration - able to influence engineering, finance, and procurement stakeholders without direct authority.

Headquarters: Remote

Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Licensed Practical Nurse) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

Schedule

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM or 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM in the Pacific time zone.

What You’ll Do

• Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

• Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways.

• Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

Who You Are

• A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

• Skilled in patient education, coaching, and care coordination - you meet patients where they are in life, considering their age, lifestyle, and diet.

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

• Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone.

• Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged.

• Comfortable using AI-assisted clinical tools (such as Gemini or Open Evidence) to support patient interactions and surface relevant clinical context, while maintaining clinical judgment as the primary guide for every patient decision.

• Biased toward action - you bring clinical authority to every interaction, make the call when it counts, and take ownership of outcomes.

What You Need

• An active compact multi-state LPN/LVN license in the state where you currently reside is required.

• At least 5 years of clinical experience as a Licensed Practical Nurse is required.

• Remote work readiness (including stable high-speed WiFi) is required.

• An active CA state LVN license is required

• Fluency in Spanish is preferred.

• Experience providing patient ed
